generated.title: Loma Prieta 1989: The Earthquake That Changed San Francisco #shorts
generated.description:
On October 17, 1989, a magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck Northern California, changing San Francisco forever.

But the story began decades earlier, with the Freeway Revolt of the 1950s and 1960s.

The earthquake damaged the Embarcadero Freeway, devastated Oakland's Cypress Street Viaduct, and forced San Francisco to confront a difficult choice: rebuild its elevated highways or transform the city.

Discover how the Loma Prieta earthquake helped reshape the Embarcadero waterfront and Hayes Valley.
